4714: Rule 37 discovery sanction dismissing the patent infringement complaint with prejudice for repeated failure to comply with discovery and case-management obligations, plus denial of reconsideration and clarification motions; the Eleventh Circuit applied regional circuit law and found no abuse of discretion or plain error.
4720: Striking the fourth set of infringement contentions under Patent Local Rule 3-1 and dismissing the action with prejudice for repeated noncompliance.

The district court properly exercised its discretion in striking Mr. Huang's contentions and dismissing the action with prejudice based on its finding that Mr. Huang repeatedly failed to serve contentions that complied with the Patent Local Rules.
4721: Denial of Huang's Rule 11 motion for sanctions against MediaTek USA and its outside counsel over alleged misrepresentations of corporate ownership.
We conclude that the district court did not abuse its discretion in holding that sanctions against MediaTek USA and its outside counsel were not warranted.
4726: Trial and case management: discovery and evidentiary rulings by the Board (redacted OPM material, allegedly false statements) were within its discretion with no substantial prejudice shown.
Therefore, we conclude no abuse of discretion occurred in this instance.
4735: Refusal of the district court to consider ChargePoint's submitted declarations under Rule 12(d) when deciding the Rule 12(b)(6) motion; no error found.
we see no error in the court's decision to decide the motion in the form it was presented.
4736: Dismissal with prejudice and entry of judgment on the same day without leave to amend; no basis found to vacate the dismissal with prejudice.
we see no basis to vacate the district court's dismissal with prejudice where ChargePoint never sought leave to amend pre-judgment
4751: Denial of Arctic Cat's motion for additional discovery (deposition testimony of Polaris employees) in the inter partes review; Board found Arctic Cat did not show the information could not be obtained otherwise under the interests-of-justice standard.
Arctic Cat did not meet its burden and, therefore, the Board did not abuse its discretion in denying the motion on that ground.
4759: Partial new trial: the court ordered a new trial on both infringement and validity of claim 10 on Alere's cross-appeal request for a validity retrial.
Accordingly, we remand for a new trial on both infringement and validity of claim 10 under the correct construction of the “equivalent to” limitation.
4783: Denial of Dobyns' Rule 60 motion for relief from the judgment, including the request to reopen for sanctions and fees; the court held Rule 60(b) cannot be used to seek sanctions and relief would be an empty exercise.
Dobyns seeks to reopen the judgment only to seek sanctions and attorney's fees. But Rule 60(b) cannot be used to seek sanctions.
4810: Denial of Fraunhofer's motion for leave to amend its complaint; court reversed, holding the amendment should have been allowed.
Under these circumstances we think the amendment should have been allowed.
4819: Trial conduct: whether Citrix's comparison of its GoToMyPC product to its prior art BuddyHelp product, and the jury instructions, required a new trial for prejudice.
We also reject Communique's assertion that the comparisons Citrix made between GoToMyPC and BuddyHelp were devastatingly prejudicial to the integrity of the trial.
4820: Evidentiary ruling: the district court allowed the PTO reexamination record at trial but barred the jury from learning that Citrix requested the reexamination.

We conclude, moreover, that the trial court did not abuse its discretion in ruling that while the PTO reexamination record could be used at trial, the jury could not be informed that Citrix was the party that requested the reexamination.
4830: Motion in limine excluding all evidence of post-March 3, 2011 inducement (and related exclusion of Johnson testimony) was reversed as an improper foreclosure of the claim.
Accordingly, we reverse the district court’s decision to preclude TecSec from introducing evidence of post-March 3, 2011 inducement of infringement.
4831: Jury Instruction No. 25 on Adobe's admitted direct infringement (the February 2009 blog post) was upheld against TecSec's challenge.

We therefore find no reversible error in Jury Instruction No. 25, without foreclosing the district court, in any new trial on inducement after March 3, 2011, from considering whether the instruction should be modified.
4832: Jury Instruction No. 28 on mere inaction not constituting inducement was upheld against TecSec's challenge.
TecSec does not contest the accuracy of Jury Instruction No. 28 as a statement of the law, and it has not shown that instruction was misleading.
4841: Discovery and privilege ruling: Board sustained the agency's attorney-client privilege claim over undated draft disciplinary proposals; court reversed because the agency made no showing of privilege and remanded for production of withheld documents.
We therefore reverse the Board's privilege ruling and remand for Mr. Siler to receive any documents withheld as privileged over his objection.
4844: Denial of leave to file a second amended complaint (failure to comply with local rule and failure to cure deficiencies)
we find that the district court did not abuse its discretion in denying Dr. Arunachalam's motion for leave to amend the complaint for a second time.
4847: Denial of motions to recuse Judge Andrews and Chief Judge Stark
we find that the district court did not abuse its discretion in denying recusal of Judge Andrews.
4850: Trial and case management: exclusion of the Poret survey as unreliable evidence, reviewed for abuse of discretion and upheld.
It was not an abuse of discretion to conclude such unreliable evidence lacks probative value.
4851: Trial and case management: Board's refusal to take judicial notice of Omaha Steaks' trademark lawsuits, upheld as harmless or within discretion.
Under the circumstances of this case, we cannot say the Board abused its discretion in failing to take judicial notice.
4859: Contempt of stipulated protective order and sanctions for violating it (including fee award and retraction order); district court's contempt finding affirmed
We do not find that the district court abused its discretion in holding EnzymeWorks in contempt for violating the stipulated protective order.
4881: Denial of Appellants' RCFC 56(d) request for discovery on the stipulation and Tax Court decision, reviewed for abuse of discretion; denial affirmed.
Here, the Claims Court correctly found that all material facts were already before the court, as it had the stipulation, Tax Court Decision, and Appellants' tax account information to review.
4994: Trial and case management: the Claims Court's denial of the taxpayers' motion for class certification as moot, after ruling against them on the merits, was affirmed.
Thus, we find that the Claims Court did not err in denying the Taxpayers’ motion for class certification as moot.
5036: Board's evidentiary ruling declining to consider paragraphs of Dr. Karger's reply declaration raising a new obviousness argument; the abuse-of-discretion ruling favored the patent owner.
The Board did not abuse its discretion in declining to consider the cited paragraphs in Dr. Karger’s reply declaration.
5043: Whether the district court abused its discretion in dismissing the suit under Rule 19(b) rather than letting it proceed in UT's absence; the court reversed and held the suit may proceed.
Given this clear factual record, we conclude that it was an abuse of discretion to find that the suit may not proceed in UT's absence.
5053: Admission of evidence of the prior Vonage jury verdict, limited by instruction to damages and willfulness, and alleged inflammatory use by counsel; district court's evidentiary rulings upheld.
we are satisfied that counsel did not make improper or inflammatory use of the Vonage evidence, and that the district court did not commit reversible error in failing to strike that evidence
5067: Evidentiary ruling: admission of Amgen's damages expert Dr. Heeb's testimony under Daubert over Hospira's objection, upheld for abuse of discretion review.
Accordingly, the district court did not abuse its discretion in permitting Dr. Heeb to testify.
5069: Trial management: denial of Amgen's new trial motion over Hospira's demonstrative during closing argument, affirmed.
It was within the district court's discretion to allow the demonstrative at issue and we do not find any abuse of discretion in the district court's denial of a new trial.
5102: Trial and case management: Board's denial of Ashe's motion for sanctions based on HHS's untimeliness was not an abuse of discretion.
we will not second guess the Board's decision absent a showing that the Board's "abuse of discretion is clear and . . . harmful."
5118: Exclusion of the partially translated and late-submitted LSI financial statement under the translation regulation and submission deadlines.
For those reasons, we affirm the Trade Court with respect to OF's challenge to Commerce's rejection of the LSI materials.
5204: Evidentiary ruling: court declined to take judicial notice of a 2017 extra-record scientific article.
Therefore, we decline to take judicial notice of the 2017 Article.
5205: Case management: special master's denial of an evidentiary hearing was within her discretion.
we conclude that the Chief Special Master acted within her discretion in denying the Olivers' request for such a hearing.
5214: Evidentiary ruling: admission of evidence about reasons for license revocation at the Board; any error harmless.
Therefore, even if the AJ had erred in admitting the evidence, any such error would be harmless.
5243: Trial and case management: denial of leave to file a second amended complaint as futile.
We agree with the Claims Court and therefore likewise decline the plaintiffs' request to amend.
5270: Sealing and unsealing of a Daubert order in district court litigation: the court vacated the unsealing order and remanded because the district court did not perform the required public-access balancing analysis.

Therefore, we vacate the Unsealing Order and remand for the district court to "make particularized determinations as to whether and, if so, to what extent" the third-party licensing information raised by Finjan should be made public.
5370: Summary judgment of non-infringement was procedurally improper because the MDL court granted it on a ground (absence of evidence of actual infringing use) that Brainlab never asserted and on which NeuroGrafix had no notice; the court reversed and remanded.

A court cannot grant summary judgment on a ground that was neither asserted by the movant nor made the subject of judicial action under Rule 56(f) that gave the nonmovant proper notice of the ground and of the obligation "to come forward with all of her evidence."
5371: The MDL court's apparent holding that Brainlab's advertisements and manual do not induce infringement as a matter of law was procedurally improper because Brainlab's motion did not argue that ground; the court reversed on that ground as well.
For the same reason, the MDL court's apparent holding that Brainlab's advertisements and manual do not induce infringement as a matter of law also was procedurally improper.
5407: Admission of Mylan's reply evidence on reasonable expectation of success in the IPR; court found no abuse of discretion in the Board's evidentiary rulings.
We see no abuse of discretion in the Board's rulings in this regard.
5420: Discovery sanctions: entry of default judgment cancelling Kaszuba's registration for willful failure to comply with discovery orders
Accordingly, we conclude that the Board did not abuse its discretion in entering default judgment against Kaszuba.
5425: Denial of leave to amend the complaint after dismissal; no abuse of discretion because amendment was never requested.
We will not find an abuse of discretion on the part of the trial court with respect to a request for amendment never made to it.
5456: Admission of expert testimony referencing life-of-relationship average customer revenue; no reversible error in denying new trial, with Hughes found to have forfeited or failed to show prejudice.

In these circumstances, whether as a matter of forfeiture or as a matter of insufficiency of a showing of prejudice from the Elbit testimony under the principle invoked by Hughes, we see no reversible error in the district court's refusal to grant a new trial.
5474: Discovery, evidentiary and hearing-continuance rulings by the Board, which the court held fall within the Board's sound discretion.
Procedural matters relative to discovery and evidentiary issues fall within the sound discretion of the board and its officials.
5503: Trial and case management: the Board's denial of discovery and an evidentiary hearing before dismissing the IRA appeal was upheld.
For none of the allegations addressed was discovery or an evidentiary hearing needed before the Board could reach its conclusion.
5530: Daubert exclusion of much of ST's expert testimony on causation and damages, reviewed for abuse of discretion and affirmed.

We have reviewed the district court's analysis closely and are satisfied that the district court did not abuse the broad discretion it is accorded in determining whether, and to what extent, to admit particular expert testimony at trial.
5540: Denial of a new trial on the ground that the defense expert gave mistaken testimony about Fottinger and on the refused anticipatory-ranges jury instruction (harmless error).
we cannot conclude that Dr. Block's misstatements warrant a new trial.
5587: Leave to amend after final judgment: court found no abuse of discretion in denying Grecia leave to amend and declined to remand for amendment.
we see no abuse of discretion in the district court's decision to deny Grecia leave to amend because he failed to describe or attach an amended complaint to his request for leave
5590: Trial and case management: the administrative judge did not abuse discretion in admitting the VA's belated closing statement, treating it as a waiver of a minor procedural violation.

5604: Rule 56(d) request for additional discovery; the court held the district court abused its discretion in denying discovery and directed discovery on remand.
On remand, we direct the district court to allow discovery as requested by ArcelorMittal under Rule 56(d) in its opposition to summary judgment.
5614: Trial and case management — district court's decision to resubmit the jury verdict form and dismiss invalidity counterclaims without prejudice, denying Rule 59(e) motion.
We conclude that the district court was within its discretion to dismiss Globus's invalidity counterclaims without prejudice.
5670: Trial management: Board did not abuse its discretion in excluding two additional witnesses as repetitious.
We find under these circumstances the Board did not abuse its discretion in excluding the testimony of the two witnesses.
5674: Trial and case management: Board's discretion to limit re-cross examination and additional witness testimony at the hearing was upheld.
The Board was therefore well within its discretion to limit additional witness examination and testimony.
5714: Trial conduct: references to GSK's total U.S. sales and 'pennies on the dollar' argument; denial of new trial on prejudicial remarks.
We therefore decline to conclude that the district court abused its discretion, and we uphold the court's decision denying a new trial on this ground.
5720: Trial evidence ruling: exclusion of the 2011 email as hearsay/lacking foundation was not an abuse of discretion.
Second, there is a lack of foundation for this exclusion.
5721: Conditional grant of a new trial on the ground that the jury verdict was against the weight of the evidence; not an abuse of discretion.

5755: Trial and case management: inherent-authority sanctions against the government and DOJ attorney Bigler for violating the duty of candor to the tribunal; the Federal Circuit held the record did not support sanctions and reversed the sanctions order.

we do not believe that the record reveals a sufficient basis for finding "the conscious doing of wrong because of dishonest purpose or moral obliquity" that is required in order to support the imposition of sanctions under the court's inherent authority.
5758: Denial of leave to file a second amended complaint: the court held the district court abused its discretion in denying leave to amend without explanation because the proposed allegations would not be futile, and reversed the denial.
Therefore, it was an abuse of discretion for the district court to deny leave to amend.
5778: Evidentiary rulings on damages: exclusion of non-commercialized prior art was an abuse of discretion, while exclusion of mulching mower prior art and evidence of delayed suit was upheld.
We conclude that the district court abused its discretion by holding that prior art is relevant to damages only to the extent that the prior art was commercialized.
5841: Request for access to an internal security office investigation report and a new hearing based on discovery; the court found no material prejudice and denied relief.
we are not persuaded that Mr. Trinkl was materially prejudiced at the hearing by not having access to the alleged report.
5856: Trial and case management: the court held the district court did not need a claim construction hearing or order, and no hearing was required before ruling on the Rule 12(b)(6) motion.
The district court did not need to hold a claim construction hearing or issue a claim construction order because Panasonic did not dispute Burnett's proposed constructions
5895: Dismissal with prejudice under Fed. R. Civ. P. 8 and 41(b) for failure to comply with the court's order to file a conforming amended complaint

We do not see any error in the district court's thorough evaluation of the Complaint or its decision to dismiss the Complaint in view of Dr. Arunachalam's failure to comply with the court's instructions.
5961: Watson's Rule 59 motion to reopen the infringement judgment after amending its ANDA process was denied; no abuse of discretion.
We agree with Indivior that the district court did not abuse its discretion.
6012: Rule 60(b)(6) relief from a final judgment on laches: the district court's denial of relief rested on Aukerman, which the Supreme Court had since overruled; the judgment was vacated and remanded to decide whether extraordinary circumstances exist.
That judgment is accordingly vacated, and this case is remanded to the district court to determine whether the "extraordinary circumstances" showing required under Rule 60(b)(6) has been established.
6013: Board expunged the patent owner's late-filed full deposition transcript as unauthorized under 37 C.F.R. 42.7(a); court held no abuse of discretion in trial/evidentiary management.
Given the strong statute-based interest in expedition in inter partes reviews, we see no basis for deeming the Board's expungement decision in this case to be an abuse of discretion.
6024: Jury instructions and denial of new trial: GMS's challenges to the ordinary observer and prior-art instructions were rejected as unpreserved or without error, so the denial of a new trial was affirmed.

6032: Denial of IMS's motion to exclude portions of Micron's Baker Reply Declaration; the court held the Board did not abuse its discretion in denying exclusion.
Accordingly, the Board did not abuse its discretion in denying IMS's motion to exclude portions of the Baker Reply Declaration.
6045: Government's motion for sanctions against Walby under Rule 38 and I.R.C. 7482(c)(4) for a frivolous appeal; the court denied the motion.
We decline to impose sanctions on Walby in this instance, however, because her filing of this frivolous appeal may be attributable to her ignorance of the law.
6067: Evidentiary ruling excluding Altaire's Reply exhibits (1027 and 1028) on TMQC-247 testing; court held exclusion was an abuse of discretion and directed the PTAB to consider the information on remand.
We conclude that the PTAB abused its discretion by refusing to consider Altaire's Reply evidence.
6122: Case management ruling on the timing of Cellspin's pleading amendment, which the district court faulted as aggressive litigation; the court held that finding clearly erroneous because the amendment was timely under the scheduling order.
The district court's finding that the timing of Cellspin's amendment contributed to making the case exceptional is therefore clearly erroneous.
6147: Exclusion of the government's expert Dr. Parsons under Fed. R. Evid. 702 based on credibility, and denial of redirect examination; the court held the exclusion was reversible error.
it was error to exclude the testimony of the government's expert.
6148: Reassignment of the case to a different judge on remand to preserve the appearance of fairness.
We think that this is one of those rare cases where reassignment is appropriate on remand.
6159: Exclusion of CalAmp's state-of-mind testimony from Chen and outside counsel Bailey on inducement and willfulness, held an abuse of discretion and substantially prejudicial

the district court's erroneous exclusion of Gallin Chen's and David Bailey's testimony as to CalAmp's state of mind substantially prejudiced CalAmp's ability to present its defense for indirect infringement.
6169: Dismissal of the later duplicative appeal in the interest of adjudicatory efficiency because an earlier appeal on the same claim remained pending before the full Board.
an administrative judge does not violate the law in dismissing the later appeal in the interest of adjudicatory efficiency
6204: Denial of Swagway's consent order motion to terminate the trademark portion of the investigation as a case management ruling; the denial was upheld as within the ALJ's discretion.
Because at that stage in the investigation the public interest in avoiding unnecessary litigation could no longer weigh in favor of granting the motion, the ALJ denied it.
6221: Rule 702 exclusion of Parallel's customer-use survey and related expert testimony for lack of fit to the claims
We are not persuaded that the district court abused its discretion by excluding Parallel's survey evidence.
6231: New trial on infringement: court held Network-1 was prejudiced by the erroneous construction and is entitled to a new trial on infringement, vacating the non-infringement judgment.
We conclude that Network-1 established that it was prejudiced by the district court's erroneous claim construction of "main power source" and is entitled to a new trial on infringement.
6245: Admissibility of the Neal Survey over Medtronic's objection that it did not name the accused VCM kit, reviewed for abuse of discretion.
We do not think, however, that Medtronic has shown error in the admission of or reliance on the survey as reasonably indicating the amount of activity by surgeons that would infringe.
6248: Discovery and case management: denial of the Rule 56(d) request for additional discovery before responding to the summary judgment motion.
The district court did not abuse its discretion by denying Super-Sparkly's request under Rule 56(d) and entering summary judgment of noninfringement.
6267: Denial of Refaei's informal request for jurisdictional discovery; the court found no abuse of discretion.
Thus, the Claims Court did not abuse its discretion in denying his informal request for discovery.
6268: Failure to address Refaei's request for leave to amend, which was incorporated into a response brief; the court found no abuse of discretion and that amendment would be futile.
we agree with the Government that the Claims Court did not abuse its discretion by failing to address Dr. Refaei's request, because it was merely incorporated into a response to a motion to dismiss.
6278: Discovery: the court affirmed the Board's denial of WesternGeco's request for additional discovery on the time-bar issue.
On this record, the Board did not abuse its discretion in concluding that additional discovery was not justified.
6285: Spoliation finding: Rembrandt's control over documents destroyed by Zhone and its bad-faith failure to preserve them, found not clearly erroneous and supporting the exceptional-case determination.
On balance, we conclude that the district court's finding of spoliation was not clearly erroneous.
6321: Trial and case management: district court's striking of plaintiff's exhibits for discovery violations affirmed
Thus, the district court did not abuse its discretion in granting Huawei's motion to strike.
6371: Denial of Ms. Aviles-Wynkoop's motion asking the court to direct DoD to produce her work-related emails (discovery), which the court refused because discovery belonged before the Board.
6393: Discovery: the Court of International Trade's grant of limited discovery under Rule 56(d) rather than full discovery was not an abuse of discretion, because ICCS offered only vague assertions about needed discovery.
Here, ICCS makes only vague assertions as to why additional discovery is needed.
6399: Exclusion under Fed. R. Civ. P. 37(c)(1) and hearsay grounds of the Perdue Farms causation statement, treated as a discovery and trial-management ruling; no abuse of discretion found.
We see no abuse of discretion in that ruling.
6420: Whether the district court had to hold an evidentiary hearing before deciding to decline jurisdiction over the declaratory judgment action; the court held no hearing was required and remand was unnecessary.
Neither party requested oral argument or an evidentiary hearing.
6477: Leave to amend the complaint: denial affirmed as futile.
The district court also did not err in denying Data Scape leave to amend its complaint, finding that it would have been futile.
6538: Evidentiary requirement for consequential damages: the MSPB required receipts or doctors' notes to substantiate medical and dental expenses, and the court declined to disturb the denial.

6540: Denial of an evidentiary hearing on the petition for enforcement; the court held the MSPB did not abuse its discretion in declining a hearing.
The MSPB did not abuse its discretion in denying Mr. MacLean's request for an evidentiary hearing.
6555: Trial and case management: admission of a non-expert fact witness's lay opinion testimony on obviousness, and denial of HVO's motion for a new trial based on that admission; the court held the limiting instruction insufficient to cure the prejudice.

6598: Leave to amend the complaint after judgment: plaintiffs may file their proposed amended complaint on remand.
We deem Plaintiffs' suggested approach sensible and are aware of no reason why they should not be permitted to file their proposed amended complaint on remand.
6606: Trial and case management: Board's allowance of supplemental evidence after remand, and the unaddressed motion to strike the agency's one-day-late filing, found not to cause substantial harm
As we defer to the Board's discretion on procedural matters relative to discovery and evidentiary issues, we see no reason to overturn the Board's allowance of additional evidence.
6620: Evidentiary exclusion at MSPB: the Board abused its discretion by excluding the Tomaski email and SAIC Sherman's testimony about it as irrelevant, in a USERRA non-selection claim.
Because we hold that the MSPB abused its discretion by excluding the Tomaski email and SAIC Sherman's testimony, we vacate the MSPB's decision and remand for further proceedings.
6627: Trial and case management: denial of Waters's motion to supplement the administrative record with news reports, photographs and internal documents.
his "allegations, even if true, do not support a finding of bias sufficient to justify supplementation of the administrative record."
6637: Denial of Caesar's motion for reconsideration of the back pay dismissal, including rejection of new evidence offered with the motion.
Therefore, denial of his motion for reconsideration was appropriate.
6663: Trial and case management: the administrative judge did not abuse her discretion by declining to sua sponte reopen the record or reconvene the hearing after ROI Exhibit 21 was admitted.
We conclude that on this record, the AJ did not abuse her discretion by not reopening the hearing or the record.
6667: Trial and case management: motion to supplement the record with material submitted after briefing was denied.
We normally do not consider material submitted after briefing unless it was previously unavailable. Therefore, Landreth's motion is denied.
6680: Denial of post-judgment motions for reconsideration and alteration, preclusion of further filings, and threatened sanctions were not an abuse of discretion.
the Court of Federal Claims did not abuse its discretion by precluding further submissions and threatening sanctions should this preclusion be flouted.
6694: Denial of Rule 60(b)(6) motion to reopen a 2014 final judgment of laches-based dismissal; court held no abuse of discretion because no extraordinary circumstances were shown, including Medinol's unappealed decision not to appeal.

6708: Scope of discovery in the PTO disciplinary proceeding; court held there is no right to full Federal Rules discovery and that the ALJ allowed reasonable discovery.
there is no right to the full scope of discovery permitted under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure in a PTO disciplinary action.
6732: Trial and case management: dismissal with prejudice under C.D. Cal. Local Rule 7-12 for failure to oppose motions to dismiss, and striking of the reconsideration motion under Local Rule 7-3 for lack of a meet-and-confer statement; affirmed as no abuse of discretion.

6773: Board's refusal to admit the 40,000-page exhibit 7 in bulk for post-trial review, as an evidentiary and case-management ruling reviewed for abuse of discretion; affirmed.
We hold that the Board did not abuse its discretion in refusing to admit that exhibit.
6795: Trial and case management: the Board's decision not to reopen the record to admit expert testimony from the terminated district court proceedings was within its discretion.

6859: Denial in full of Uniloc's own motions to seal its confidential information and that of its related entities (overbroad sealing request, failure to comply with Local Rules 79-5 and 7-9), affirmed.
the district court did not abuse its discretion in denying Uniloc's motions to seal its purportedly confidential information and that of its related entities.
6860: Sealing of third-party licensee information: the district court made insufficient findings balancing public access against third-party interests, so those portions of the sealing orders were vacated and remanded for particularized determinations.

6878: Denial of Verify's discovery requests from TCH and related due process challenge, reviewed for abuse of discretion
We find that the Board's determination that Verify's motions were overbroad and untimely was reasonable and that the Board did not abuse its discretion in denying the motions.
6896: Credibility weighing of Elbit's expert testimony by the PTAB, declined to disturb.
we decline to disturb these credibility determinations here.
6952: Exclusion of prosecuting attorney testimony as untimely advice-of-counsel waiver of privilege

7042: Imposition of an anti-filing sanction (injunction requiring leave of the Chief Judge before further filings) on a pro se litigant for repeated, duplicative filings.
The Claims Court was well within its discretion when it ordered the anti-filing sanction in light of Mr. O'Diah's prior filings.
7094: Admission of evidence of the prior Vonage jury verdict and limiting instruction; counsel's references to the verdict not inflammatory
we are satisfied that counsel did not make improper or inflammatory use of the Vonage evidence, and that the district court did not commit reversible error
7122: Denial of further leave to amend as to Alcoa after repeated failure to cure deficiencies (alternative holding).
In these circumstances, we cannot say the district court abused its discretion in denying further leave to amend.
7124: Denial of leave to amend the complaint against Ball for a fourth time, with dismissal with prejudice.
In these circumstances, the district court did not abuse its discretion in denying further leave to amend.
7175: Striking of the plaintiffs' Woods declaration submitted late in the fee proceedings as untimely
We see no abuse of discretion in the district court’s striking of the Woods Declaration.
7189: Denial of Cisco's motion to supplement the post-trial record with declarations on post-verdict designaround activity, held untimely and within discretion.

7217: Board's exclusion of arguments improperly incorporated by reference from the Struhsaker declaration and claim chart under 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(a)(3), reviewed for abuse of discretion.
the Board was within its discretion in excluding the arguments made in the claim chart.

7233: Adoption of XY's proposed special verdict form on breach of contract issues
we find no abuse of discretion by the district court in adopting XY's proposed verdict form.
7247: Exclusion of Exhibit C of Dr. Lipson's declaration as an improper incorporation of arguments by reference under 37 C.F.R. 42.6(a)(3); exclusion favored the petitioner and was affirmed for lack of abuse of discretion.
we conclude that the Board did not abuse its discretion in excluding Exhibit C of Dr. Lipson's declaration.
7299: Denial of employee's request to depose agency counsel as a witness and rejection of the claimed conflict of interest in counsel's representation; court found no abuse of discretion.
the Board did not abuse its discretion in denying Mr. Hernandez's request to call Mr. Frison as a witness and in finding no conflict.
7306: Denial of Securiforce's posttrial sanctions motions for discovery failures under Court of Federal Claims Rule 37.
We see no abuse of discretion in the Claims Court's determination that sanctions were not warranted.
7315: Denial of relief from final judgment under RCFC 60(b)(6) (no extraordinary circumstances shown), coded as a trial and case management ruling because no closer code fits.

7322: Trial and case management: the district court properly granted summary judgment on a ground the movant did not expressly argue, because D Three had notice and an opportunity to respond under Rule 56(f).
we will not find a violation of Rule 56(f) here
7381: Evidentiary exclusion: Administrative Judge did not abuse discretion in excluding testimony of Reesman and Depperman as irrelevant or redundant regarding institutional motive to retaliate.
we conclude that the Administrative Judge did not abuse his discretion in excluding Mr. Reesman’s testimony.
7420: Board's entry of default judgment as a discovery sanction against Corcamore for litigation misconduct and violation of discovery and deposition orders.

14986: Approval of the class action settlement as fair, reasonable and adequate under Rule 23(e)(2), including the pro rata distribution and the $350 threshold.
Thus, we conclude that the district court acted well within its discretion in approving the settlement.
15011: Evidentiary ruling: Board's consideration of the unsigned Tax Court Stipulation and Tax Court Decision reached through settlement, under Fed. R. Evid. 408 and Board evidentiary discretion; court found no abuse of discretion and no harm.

We thus do not see any abuse of discretion in the Board's consideration of the Stipulation and Tax Court documents, and even if there had been an abuse of discretion, Ms. Harris-Campbell has not made a showing of harm or prejudice where there is no substantive dispute as to the fact that she settled with the IRS for a sum consistent with what is reflected in the Tax Court documents and Stipulation.
15020: Request for court-appointed counsel in the appeal; denied.
we deny Mr. Alvarez's request for court-appointed counsel, ECF No. 12, as there is generally no right to counsel in civil cases absent a potential loss of personal freedom.
15047: Board's rejection of additional evidence on review as not new and material under 5 C.F.R. § 1201.115(d), including record-closure timing.
Given the record closed in May 2019 and Ms. Thurston was separated from the USPS in April 2019, substantial evidence supports the Board’s finding.
15065: Denial of leave to amend the complaint: the Court of Federal Claims did not abuse its discretion because plaintiff never moved to amend.
A trial court does not abuse its discretion by not allowing a party to amend a complaint where the party fails to move to amend.
15137: Denial of motion to recall the mandate and vacate the Veterans Court judgment; no abuse of discretion found
For the same reasons that the Veterans Court properly denied relief initially, it did not err in denying the motion to recall the mandate and to vacate the judgment.
15142: Trial evidence rulings: exclusion of MaxLite authenticating witness Marsh and the DX-41 presentation held an abuse of discretion, requiring a new trial on validity of the tube patents.
Because there is no such requirement, we conclude that the exclusion of Mr. Marsh's testimony was an abuse of discretion.
15156: Evidentiary ruling: the administrative judge's admission of hearsay evidence from supervisors was upheld as within the Board's discretion.
Mr. Stenson does not show that, in these particular circumstances, the administrative judge abused her discretion in admitting the evidence.
15191: Trial and case management: representation of an entity by a non-lawyer under Claims Court Rule 83.1(a)(3) and the court's refusal to recognize the Tribe as plaintiff.
the Claims Court correctly held that under Claims Court Rule 83.1(a)(3), a non-lawyer may not represent an entity, including an Indian tribe, before the court.
15196: Denial of Fritz's motion to supplement the pleadings (leave to supplement the mandamus record) affirmed
We see no due process violation based on these facts and therefore affirm the Veterans Court's denial of Mr. Fritz's motion to supplement his pleadings.
15202: Admission of Dr. Lehrman's infringement testimony; denial of motion to strike or exclude expert testimony under Daubert
we affirm the decision to not exclude or strike the infringement testimony of Roland's technical expert
15204: Provision of non-admitted claim chart (illustrative aid) to the jury during deliberations; denial of new trial on infringement held harmless
Accordingly, inMusic cannot show that it was prejudiced.
15213: Trial court's decision to construe the government's motion to dismiss as applying to the amended complaint filed after the motion, without abuse of discretion.

The Claims Court did not abuse its discretion in construing the motion to dismiss to apply to Tindall's amended complaint, because the amended complaint contained substantially the same factual allegations as the original.
15226: Discovery: the administrative judge's denial of Etzel's motion to compel as untimely was not an abuse of discretion.
There is, in short, no clear error in AJ Alexander's interpretation of AJ Weiss' prior order and no abuse of discretion in denying the motion to compel.
15259: Trial and case management: Board's discovery, hearing and evidentiary rulings (declining a hearing sua sponte, not ordering further discovery, denying motion to supplement the record) reviewed for abuse of discretion and found proper.
Mr. Startz waived his right to a hearing, and the Board did not abuse its discretion by declining to order one sua sponte.
15274: Denial of employee's motion to suspend the merits hearing because of the video-conference format; the court held video hearings acceptable absent specific unfairness.
As such, we reject Mr. Nathan's argument that it was error to schedule a video conference.
15275: Dismissal of the appeal as a sanction for bad-faith refusal to answer questions at the prehearing conference, under 5 C.F.R. § 1201.43.
We conclude that the Board did not err in dismissing Mr. Nathan's appeal as a sanction for his conduct during the prehearing proceedings.
15316: Trial and case management: the administrative judge's exclusion of agency witness Ferguson based on the parties' stipulated facts was not an abuse of discretion.
The administrative judge did not abuse his discretion.

15341: Denial of motion to alter or amend the judgment under Rules 52(b) and 59(e)
Nor did the district court abuse its discretion by denying DS Advanced's motion to alter or amend the judgment.
15342: Discovery sanctions against counsel Cummins for violating the protective order, including finding of violation and sanction imposed
The district court did not err in finding a violation of the protective order.
15354: Trial and case management: AJ's exclusion of witness Brett Markham and denial of post-hearing briefing upheld as within discretion.
Mr. Kroenung falls far short of showing these case management decisions were an abuse of discretion.
